To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angular distribution of projectile fragment alpha in terms of the transverse momentum could be explained by two sources emission hypothesis of PS Model.
the emission of alpha particles from the projectile fragments is not only due to the contact layer or hot layer, rather it is due to two sources, one is hot and other is cold.
the emission of alpha particles from 84 Kr interactions is from two different sources and the temperature of the two sources is different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the emission of projectile fragment alpha in 84 Kr interaction with nuclei of NED’s target.

the study of two source emission behaviour of projectile fragments alpha of projectile having kinetic energy around 1.1 GeV pernucleon produced in 84Kr interactions with the nuclei in the NED at relativistic energy.
the study of the emission of projectile fragment alpha in terms of the transverse momentum in 84 Kr – NED interactions at around 1GeV per nucleon kinetic energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the projectile fragments alpha were emitted from two different sources that belong to projectile spectator region having drastically different temperatures.

projectile fragments alpha are coming from two different sources, one from the contact layer (hot source) and the other from the projectile spectator (cold source) and the temperature of hot region is dependent on the projectile’s mass number.
projectile fragments alpha are emitted from two separate sources having different temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emission of fragments alpha from two different sources has been observed.
the projectile fragments alpha are coming from two different sources having two different temperatures.
the emission of the projectile fragments alpha is coming out of two sources, the first source is the contact layer or the hot source and the second source is the cold source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emission of alpha fragments from the cold region dominates the emission of alpha from the hot source.

the transverse momentum of projectile fragments alfa produced in 84Kr interactions with NED nuclei is not a function of the emission angle but a function of the projectile mass number, target mass number and the projectile energy.

the emission of the projectile fragments alpha from the hot source in the projectile spectator region is a few percent and the majority of the projectile fragments α are emitted from the projectile cold source. [1]
